Tor is running and your address is published. Contacts who also have the app open can reach you, and you can reach them.
Tor is not ready. Nothing can be sent or received, and nothing is being held anywhere for later.
Your traffic is leaving through a VPN interface. Whospair can see that much, and no more — it does not know which provider, or whether the tunnel leaks.
Your traffic is leaving directly. Your network provider can see that this device uses Tor, and when — not who you talk to, nor what is said.

Whospair encrypts what you say, and Tor hides who you say it to. Neither hides that you use Tor: whoever carries your traffic sees it, at what times, and how often. A VPN moves that view to the tunnel operator instead. That is a real change when the party watching is the one you are worried about.
A VPN is not a guarantee. You are choosing who gets to watch, not removing the watcher. Pick one you have reason to trust, and prefer one you pay for over one that pays for itself with your traffic.
This person added you with your link. You have not confirmed who they are.

Compare it with your contact in person or by a call. Same number on both phones = no one in between.

Delete this contact and all messages? If they still have your link, they may come back as unconfirmed — block them to prevent that.
